You watch the cut, you know what is wrong, and then you try to type it into a chat box: this slow motion, that card, the cut right there.

This is the loop that fixed it for us. We used it to cut our LEGO-style short again in one night: 36 comments, 8 versions, and a tool the agent built in the first seven minutes. The tool is free and open source, and the steps work with any agent that can edit a video.

## Give yourself a way to point

Eze made a LEGO-style short for Agent Swarm: 66 seconds in a city built from bricks, about why open source matters in the time of AI and the big labs. Every clip was generated on Higgsfield . We will write a later post on how he made it. It was a tedious and manual process, on purpose, to avoid AI slop.

On the evening of November 18 he handed the project over: 16 raw clips, his voice recordings, a scripted build, and his second cut. Taras opened a session in T3 Code , on his own machine, in the repo where we render our videos. The agent was Claude Code with Claude Fable 5.2. It ran locally on purpose: we iterate faster that way. Before anything else, the agent loaded a skill to read the files of Eze from the shared drive:

loaded the skill agent-fs 22:48

Taras had notes. Ten minutes in, he stopped talking about the film:

create a little html page adhoc where i can leave comments with drawing tool on frames (ranges) in the video please so we can iterate

So the first thing the agent shipped that night was a tool. It took seven minutes. From its reply:

Taras, the review page is ready

Comments stay in the browser, so a reload does not lose them. You can edit, delete or play the range of each comment.

Click Download JSON and tell me.

Six minutes after that, Taras was reviewing the reviewer:

can you make it so that the ranges i can click in the timeline and and create them + drag and drop + move them around + right click to options? like a more proper timeline editor, also make it bigger please

Two shorter messages followed, "remove scrollbars" and "also cmd enter should create comment". By 23:23 the page had the shape it still has:

- One HTML file with no server, no build and no dependency

- A timeline where you drag to make a range, drag to move it, and drag its ends to trim it

- A pen, an arrow and a box to draw on the picture

- Comments saved in the browser, and a button that exports them as JSON

At 23:37 Taras wrote that he had left comments, and asked for more: ideas from a reference trailer. The agent got ready to hand work to subagents. It loaded two skills, then started the first subagent, a search for voices:

loaded the skills delegate-work , asd-ste100 23:37

At 23:49 the first export came back. It had 21 comments on a 66-second film. Five of them:

the slowmo is laggy, which makes it feel ugly

this should replace the subtitles no? it feels weird floating here

we should re-think the cards, make them nicer basically now the text is not aligned, feels weird...

we could think of another idea of game over? not sure what but we could iterate + needs to be centered obviously. maybe we could use some effect from some existing game

here there are like weird jump transitions from one scene to the other...

Nobody writes like that in a brief, and that is the point. With a range selected and the frame on screen, a comment can be eight words long and still be exact.

## Make every comment data

A comment is a time range, a text, and the marks drawn on the picture. This one is the comment from the clip above:

{ "n": 2, "in": "0:21.00", "out": "0:21.00", "inFrame": 504, "outFrame": 504, "startSec": 21, "endSec": 21.042, "text": "Tag sits too near the edge. Give it the same margin as the captions.", "strokes": [ { "tool": "rect", "color": "#ff3b30", "width": 0.005, "frame": 504, "points": [[0.0395, 0.0756], [0.2772, 0.2536]] }, { "tool": "arrow", "color": "#ff3b30", "width": 0.005, "frame": 504, "points": [[0.475, 0.4472], [0.2935, 0.2536]] } ] }

Frames and seconds are both there, so the agent does not convert. The points of a mark are shares of the picture: [0, 0] is the top left corner and [1, 1] is the bottom right.

A list of coordinates is a poor way to tell an agent "this thing here". So the tool comes with a short Python script that reads an export and writes one frame for each comment, with the marks drawn on it. The agent looks at the frame first and reads the words second.

The rule we wrote down afterwards: a mark shows what the words do not.

- 0:00 Three comments

- 0:01 Open a marked frame

- 0:03 Jump to a range

- 0:05 Play the range

- 0:08 Copy the JSON

## Review in rounds, and start small

Three exports came out of the tool that night and the next morning.

Round 2 is the one to copy. After round 1 the agent did not build the whole film. It showed the text pieces as stills over real frames, then built the first act completely: picture, voice, music, text. Taras approved the style on 25 seconds, and only then did the rest get built. A design that is wrong costs seconds on a still and ten minutes on a render.

## Hold the agent to three habits

The tool only carries the comments. Three habits on the agent's side made them useful.

Group by cause. Six of the 21 comments in round 1 were about slow motion: "ugly slowmo again", "weird slowmo", "slowmo". Six comments, one cause: the cut stretched clips to fit the voice. The answer was one rule, footage plays at real speed, and a decision to cut the film again from the raw clips rather than repair the render.

Ask when a comment can mean two things. Round 2, comment 1: "i would remove the tire effect and start the text a bit later". There was no tire. The agent asked which part. It was the record-scratch sound, and the answer came back as a new idea: "like if you menu paused the game you know?". The film now pauses on a game menu.

Answer "options?" with clips. A comment that asked for options got two or three built versions as short clips around the moment, one frame of each side by side, and a pick with one reason. Taras chose from things he could watch.

The comment that changed the session most was typed in the chat, not in the tool:

ask me questions before going deep to implement stuff so we align on the changes

After that, the agent asked 22 questions across 8 dialogs before it built anything large, each with a recommendation.

The agent was also wrong, and the rounds are how we found out fast. Act 1 was planned at 17 seconds and came back at 25.5, a third of it frozen frames. The ending was "meh, like too big". And one comment needs no time range to make its point:

no emdash in subtitles!!!!!!!! remove those

The build now stops when a caption has one.

## Ask what was not checked

The agent verified a lot before it showed a render: the words against the script with a transcription, blank frames, loudness, a contact sheet at two frames a second. It could not hear the voice or the music. So every message that came with a render said so, in a list of its own: what changed, what was checked, what is for your ears.

This is from the message that came with the full film:

What I checked

- Words: Scribe hears all 175 words of your script.

- Picture: no blank frames. Still frames occur only in the devices: pause menu, NPC freeze, billing block, end card.

- Loudness: -14.3 LUFS, peak at -1.4 dB.

I cannot hear the film. All music and effects after act 1 are unheard by anyone.

Points to listen and look for

- Ending music: the generator returned one ringing chord in place of a slow last phrase.

- Voice against music is tight in act 1 on lines 4, 6 and 8: about 8 dB. All other lines have 10 dB or more.

That list matters more than it looks. A reviewer who knows what was not checked knows where to listen.

Eze's cut went in at 22:48. Version 8 came out at 12:08 the next day. Taras slept for seven of those hours. Before he did, he approved the style on act 1 and wrote "continue w the other parts yolo". The agent delivered the full film at 02:36, built on the direction the comments had set so far.

## Turn the session into a skill

Version 8 came out at 12:08. Three minutes later Taras asked for the step that makes the night count twice:

ok nice, please commit and push all to the repo please. important you upload the video feedbacker too please! put it somewhere there also skillify some of the things we did in this session: general feedback loops, branding decisions, editing, etc so that next time is better

The agent wrote two chapters into the skill of our videos repo: the review loop, and a playbook for films cut from generated clips. They hold the habits above as rules, several with the words of Taras next to them. The next session starts from those chapters, not from zero.

The review chapter is public as the video-review-loop skill. Give it to your agent before your first round.

## Make the loop native

The tool was committed at 12:18. Eight minutes later Taras wrote to the lead agent of our swarm in Slack. The lead answered with a design and a name, and seven minutes after that it had a go:

hey check in github.com/desplega-ai/agent-swarm-videos specially the tools/video-review/README.md

thinking if you could create a page replicating that, but w agent-fs native integration

essentially you could select a video (or auto set via query params) and then leave feedback (autosaved in some agent-fs location)

then you could have a way to link that video feedback iteration to a native swarm task thread so you could "send to swarm" with links to tasks and session

wdyt? as it's a super powerful tool for the back and forth

Worth building, as an App: ?path= loads the agent-fs video, comments autosave next to it, "Send to swarm" opens a task, and later cuts chain via parentTaskId . Say "go" and Picateclas builds it.

go, use hive styling and branding but keep it pretty similar, it needs to be clean af

Lead told Picateclas to use the skill apps 12:34

Picateclas is one of our worker agents. It built the page, the app and the script behind them in about 21 minutes, and reported what it had left out:

Video Review is live and tested end to end.

Skipped/risk: the reviewer is a Page, since apps can't seek video. Saves use my agent identity.

The reviewer is the same. What changed is everything around it.

That last row is the one we wanted. The agent that applies a round writes the new cut next to the old one and answers with a review link. A round sent from that link is a child of the agent's own task. Every round of one video ends up in one thread, with the session of each.

Four hours later, another team was making videos with their own swarm, and Taras asked the lead to share the tool. A worker packaged it in under six minutes: an install script, the app definition, the page, and a small skill that teaches agents how to open a video, read the feedback and answer a round.
